summary: I found nothing to refute in this record: the identity and capability facts I checked all hold. Things I read myself: the HF API (createdAt 2025-05-29, which puts it outside the window; 8,190,735,360 BF16 params; 16.38 GB; MIT tag), config.json, README, the chat template in tokenizer_config.json and tokenizer.json. The DeepSeek tool tokens are absent from the vocab. The official template never renders tool definitions. vLLM v0.33.0 marks the DeepSeek R1 series 'Tool Calling ❌', and its deepseek_v3 tool parser raises a RuntimeError when those tokens are missing. Every vendor benchmark (86.0/76.3/61.5/61.1/60.5) matches the card and is self-reported. The agentic numbers (SWE-bench, BFCL, Tau-Bench) belong to the 671B model, as the record says. All Artificial Analysis values match the page payload (tau2 0, Terminal-Bench Hard 0.0152, LCB 0.513, AIME25 0.637, GPQA 0.612, IFBench 0.199, HLE 0.059, LCR 0.15). The Ollama 8b template has no Tools block and honours think. I re-derived the memory arithmetic and got the same results. Minor corrections only: (1) the list of in-window deepseek-ai repos leaves out DeepSeek-OCR-2 (3.39B, OCR vision model), Math-V2 (685B) and V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, none of which changes the conclusion; (2) JamAndTea FP8 is 9.44 GB and unsloth bnb is 7.44 GB (rounding); (3) Ollama's think=false text has a trailing newline pair; (4) the Qwen <tool_call> token (id 151657) is present in the vocab, so it is worth noting for any hermes-style experiment. Gaps: I did not check that the unsloth template derives from sglang, I could not pin the AA Intelligence Index version, and I ran no end-to-end tool-call test. The verdict stands: thinking-only, no dependable tool calling, unsuitable as an OpenCode agent.
